Physics and astronomy
Physics and astronomy
Explore and understand the science behind our world and universe, from the atomic and subatomic scale all the way to stars and galaxies. Learn how this central science underpins ideas in fields such as electronics, lasers, music and semiconductors.
St Andrews is home to state-of-the-art research labs and its own observatory with the largest operational telescope in Scotland.

Joint degree options
You can take the Physics BSc, Physics MPhys and Theoretical Physics MPhys programmes with another subject as part of a joint degree. Find out more about taking a joint Honours degree.
Supported pathways
These courses provide supported entry into degree-level study for applicants who do not meet the minimum entry grades, but meet contextual criteria.
Gateway to Science (pathway to BSc or MPhys)
FE-HE Pathway to Science (pathway to BSc Hons)
International Foundation programmes
International Foundation programmes enable international students from a wide range of countries to develop the necessary skills to meet the demands of an undergraduate degree programme across subjects and disciplines at the University of St Andrews.

Postgraduate research
The School of Physics and Astronomy offers PhD and MSc (res) research opportunities in the following areas:
astrophysics
condensed matter
photonics
Read more on postgraduate research opportunities.
To apply, you should first identify and contact a potential supervisor you would like to work with in your intended research area.
“I wanted to study at a university with excellent teaching and lots of contact with the actual research in the field. I could not have made a better choice! Studying Physics is undeniably hard, however the supportive atmosphere in the School, the excitement about the subject and the great people who I do it with are worth it.”

School of Physics and Astronomy
The School of Physics and Astronomy provides teaching excellence through small class sizes and accessible staff who enjoy explaining the excitement of physics and astronomy to students. The School has research expertise in astrophysics, condensed matter, and photonics.
Studying in St Andrews
Entry requirements
The University offers a variety of flexible entry options in order to allow all students, regardless of background or personal circumstances, to apply.
Fees and funding
Scholarships and funding options are available at every level of study.
Accommodation
St Andrews has variety of accommodation options to suit all tastes and budgets.
Visit St Andrews
If you’re interested in studying at St Andrews, join us at a visiting day or talk and tour to explore the town, find out about our courses and meet current students. You can also join us for one of our upcoming online events.
